original_statement:
What must hold? State the invariant or expectation this concerns. contracts/specs/derived-arn-5db.spec.json clause c2: running forge test executes a check for the S6 rule and fails the suite when a forbidden name is present in the adjudicator source, so the forge suite is itself the enforcement, not an unexercised side script. docs/ORACLES.md section 9: an oracle must not report a verdict it did not compute.
What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. On integrated df56543, clause c2 of derived-arn-5db runs python3 scripts/check-settlement-rate-free-gate.py. The script contains no subprocess or os.system call. On a scan without findings it prints the literal {"series": [[0, 0], [1, 1]]} (scripts/check-settlement-rate-free-gate.py:117) and exits 0. On 2026-10-15, in a worktree at integrated, the script printed {"series": [[0, 0], [1, 1]]} with exit 0, and after git rm test/SettlementRateFree.t.sol it printed the same output with exit 0. arn-5db closed on 2026-10-15 with this clause graded as passed.
How do you see it? Describe exactly how to observe this for yourself — the steps to reproduce, or how you would demo it. 1. git worktree add <dir> integrated. 2. In <dir> run python3 scripts/check-settlement-rate-free-gate.py and record stdout and exit code. 3. git rm test/SettlementRateFree.t.sol, run the script again, and compare: the output and exit code are the same. 4. Read scripts/check-settlement-rate-free-gate.py:89-123.
Where does this apply? (e.g. gateway route, mobile screen, CLI verb) scripts/check-settlement-rate-free-gate.py (oracle of derived-arn-5db clause c2)
restatement: The acceptance oracle that exophial runs to grade clause c2 of derived-arn-5db must compute its pass or fail verdict from forge test's real execution of the enforcing Solidity test, not from an independent Python re-implementation of the same source scan. Today scripts/check-settlement-rate-free-gate.py scans src/ArmadaNitroAdjudicator.sol and every .sol file under src/nitro/ for the forbidden names ERC4626, IERC4626, convertToAssets, convertToShares, and preview entirely in Python, with no subprocess or os.system call to forge anywhere in the script. Because of this, deleting test/SettlementRateFree.t.sol, the forge test that clause c2 requires as the real enforcement, does not change the script's output: it still prints {"series": [[0, 0], [1, 1]]} and exits 0, exactly as it does when that test file is present. The oracle therefore reports that forge test enforces the rule, a fact it never computed, which violates docs/ORACLES.md section 9: an oracle must not report a verdict it did not compute. The fix must make the check's result track forge test's real outcome for the SettlementRateFreeTest contract, so deleting test/SettlementRateFree.t.sol causes the check to report failure instead of the false pass it reports today.

restatement_clauses.text: scripts/check-settlement-rate-free-gate.py must compute its pass or fail result from forge test's real execution of the SettlementRateFreeTest contract in test/SettlementRateFree.t.sol, so that deleting test/SettlementRateFree.t.sol causes the check to report failure instead of the {"series": [[0, 0], [1, 1]]} pass it reports today.

goal: Make the clause-c2 gate depend on forge test actually running the enforcing test, so deleting the enforcing test file is caught as a failure instead of a silent pass.
acceptance_criteria: Run the check twice against two throwaway copies of the repository: one with the forge test file test/SettlementRateFree.t.sol in place, and one with that file deleted. The first run reports a passing result, same as today. The second run, with the enforcing test gone, now reports a failing result instead of the same passing result it reports today.
